reproduction_target: An entirely in-silico machine-learning study by Eigen Bio Inc.: (1) statistical characterisation of a compendium of 3,079 quality-controlled plasma cfRNA samples drawn from 35 studies via the authors' own 'cfRNA Codex' atlas (gene-wise dropout fractions, percentile-aligned cross-study dropout correlation, heavy-tailed log-normal/Pareto fits, method-of-moments negative-binomial dispersion, library-size perturbation, gene-gene Pearson correlation and PCA); (2) construction of a cfRNA-aware Structural Causal Model synthetic task generator (latent factors, log-normal abundance with CV-percentile-calibrated variance, Bernoulli dropout, Poisson sequencing noise, library-size normalisation, Linear/MLP/Tree structural equation families); (3) validation that the synthetic prior universe recovers the real-data statistics; (4) meta-training of cfRNA-ICL, a TabICL-derived in-context-learning transformer with a modified gene-wise embedding stage, row-wise interaction module and asymmetric support/query cross-attention; (5) downstream benchmarking against a generically pretrained TabICL on K = 16 classification tasks derived from GEO GSE183635, plus few-shot evaluation at n = 5, 10, 20, 50 and a UMAP analysis of row-level embeddings across five cancer types. There are no wet-lab steps performed in this work; all data are pre-existing public or in-house sequencing archives.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-analysis, built from the bioRxiv v1 JATS source XML (fetched with curl and a browser User-Agent; WebFetch returned HTTP 403 for the JATS URL). The paper has NO Data Availability statement, NO Code Availability statement, and NO software repository of any kind, so there is no README prose and no repo landing page to read. The only Declarations entry is a Competing Interest statement ('Authors are employees or founders of Eigen Bio Inc.'). Not a single software package, library or version is named anywhere in the Methods: no deep-learning framework, no UMAP implementation, no numerical/statistics library, no random seed. TabICL and TabPFN appear only as arXiv citations of prior architectures, not as pinned dependencies. Several Results-section analyses (percentile-aligned dropout comparison, NB dispersion fit, library-size perturbation, correlation/PCA) are described only in the Results narrative rather than in a dedicated Methods subsection; they are still counted as computational steps because they produce reported numbers. Layer W = 0: no physical or observational step is performed in this study.
capture_claim_note: Unambiguous 'none'. The paper claims no lockfile, no container, no conda/pip environment, no release snapshot, and not even a floating tool name with a version-like string. Zero software artifacts of any kind are asserted. capture_claim 'floating' was considered and rejected because 'floating' presupposes that named-but-unpinned tools exist; here no tool is named at all in the Methods, so there is nothing to float. stage2_candidate is therefore false.

steps.label: Assembly and quality control of the cfRNA compendium: 3,079 QC-passed plasma cfRNA samples from 35 independent studies (281-139,343 genes per dataset), drawn from the authors' own 'cfRNA Codex' resource (>15,000 samples, cited as Kim et al. 2025, DOI 10.13140/RG.2.2.34492.71042) - no QC criteria, no study list, no sample manifest, no software

Gene-wise dropout / zero-fraction computation per study, cross-study comparison by a 'percentile-alignment approach', mean cross-study Pearson correlation rho = 0.733, plus heavy-tailed (log-normal and Pareto) fits to the dropout distribution - percentile-alignment procedure and fitting method not specified, no software

Negative-binomial overdispersion characterisation: fraction of genes with variance > 2x mean (51.8%) and a global dispersion parameter theta = 1.61 fitted by method-of-moments across genes with non-zero expression - estimator stated, gene-filtering and normalisation of the input matrix not stated, no software

Library-size / compositional-shift analysis: library sizes reported from 13,519 to 1.1e11 reads (median 467,811, mean 116 million) and multiplicative library-size perturbation at 0.5x, 1x, 2x with observation of movement along dominant axes of variation - perturbation factors given, the 'dominant axes' projection method not specified, no software

Gene-gene correlation structure and PCA: pairwise Pearson correlations on log-transformed, library-size-normalised expression across all gene pairs within each study (median |rho| = 0.388, mean 0.304, Q25-Q75 [0.175, 0.613]); PCA reporting PC1 explaining 68.3% of variance on average - log transform offset, normalisation constant, gene filtering and PCA implementation all unstated

cfRNA-aware Structural Causal Model task generator: K latent root causes with clipped Gaussian gene loadings, structural equation families (Linear / small MLP / decision tree), log-normal pre-dropout abundance with sigma^2 mapped from empirical CV percentiles via CV^2 = exp(sigma^2) - 1, abundance-independent Bernoulli dropout with gene-specific p_j from Codex detect rates, Poisson sequencing noise with lambda fixed to 1, and CPM-like library-size normalisation with scaling constant s - equations given in prose but K, clipping bounds, family mixture weights, MLP/tree hyperparameters, library-size distribution and s are all left symbolic (several display equations are also absent from the JATS text stream)

Meta-learning task construction: per-task support/query split with the latent regression score r_i produced by a decision function M drawn from the same Linear/MLP/Tree families as the gene mechanisms; 'sample and feature dimensions vary across tasks' - the ranges for N, G, support size and query size are stated only as a display equation that is not present in the text, and the label thresholding / class-balance rule is not described

Statistical-fidelity validation of the synthetic prior universe against real cfRNA: synthetic median zero fraction 97.4%, dropout rank concordance Spearman rho = 0.960, 75.1% of synthetic genes above the 2x variance-over-mean threshold, CV-distribution comparison - number of synthetic tasks/datasets sampled, seed, and the matching procedure not stated, no software

cfRNA-ICL architecture definition and meta-training on the SCM prior universe: gene-wise embedding E_phi (detect-rate smoothing with a learned small-mass surrogate, log-plus variance stabilisation calibrated to empirical CV, gene-specific dispersion scaling), RowMix row-wise interaction (lightweight MLP + low-rank attention + dropout-aware gating), dataset-level asymmetric cross-attention (support-support attention allowed, query-query attention restricted), two-layer MLP output head - no layer counts, no hidden or embedding dimensions, no attention head counts, no optimiser, learning rate, batch size, number of meta-training steps/tasks, no hardware, no framework, no seed, no checkpoint release

Baseline TabICL model pretrained on generic synthetic data, used as the sole comparator ('both models undergo identical fine-tuning procedures') - TabICL appears only as an arXiv citation (Qu et al. 2025, arXiv:2502.05564); no checkpoint identity, no version, no fine-tuning protocol, no hyperparameters

Downstream benchmark evaluation: K = 16 classification tasks constructed from GEO GSE183635 (10 all-stage binary cancer-detection tasks + 6 early-stage tasks, class imbalance ~1:1 to 4:1), reporting accuracy, ROC-AUC (88.35% -> 90.52%) and F1 (46.73% -> 52.75%) - accession is public and cited with URL, but the per-task sample selection, healthy-control definition, stage assignment, preprocessing of the GEO matrix, train/test splitting and repetition count are not stated, and no evaluation code exists

Few-shot / low-sample generalisation evaluation at n = 5, 10, 20, 50 labelled examples on the same GSE183635 tasks (e.g. 66.4% vs 53.1% accuracy at n = 5; 75.6% vs 59.4% at n = 10) - the support-set sampling scheme, number of random repeats, and variance estimation are not stated

Representation-level analysis: extraction of row-level embeddings from the feature-interaction module and UMAP projection of real cfRNA samples spanning five cancer types (breast, cholangiocarcinoma, colorectal, glioma, head and neck) - no UMAP implementation, no n_neighbors / min_dist / metric / random_state, no sample counts per cancer type

headline.static_readiness: 0/13 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: X on all 13/13 computational steps. This is a floor case, not a ceiling case: the version axis is 0 for every step because the paper names no software package, library, framework or version anywhere, so no step can rise above X even if every other axis were maximal. The code axis is additionally 0 on 6/13 steps (C1 compendium QC, C9 architecture/meta-training, C10 TabICL baseline, C11-C13 evaluation and UMAP) because no repository, no model checkpoint, and no hyperparameter values are provided - these steps are not reconstructable from prose. The single strongest artifact in the paper is the public GEO accession GSE183635 used for downstream benchmarking (data = 2 on C11-C13); the meta-training data source (cfRNA Codex) is an in-house atlas released only as a companion DOI with no deposit, giving data = 1 on the compendium/SCM-calibration steps and data = 0 where the input is purely synthetic and unarchived. No stage-2 verification is warranted: there is nothing to verify.
headline.coverage: 13 computational steps assessed from the bioRxiv v1 JATS Methods and Results prose. W = 0: the study performs no wet-lab or observational work; all inputs are pre-existing sequencing archives (GEO GSE183635) or synthetic data generated by the described SCM. Note that reference [19] describes GSE183635 as 'tumor-educated platelet RNA' while the paper uses it as a cfRNA benchmark; this modality-labelling discrepancy is recorded here for the record but is a validity question, not a readiness axis, and no verdict was adjusted for it.

gaps.where: Whole paper (no Declarations section beyond Competing Interest)
gaps.missing: No code availability statement and no code repository of any kind (GitHub / GitLab / Bitbucket / Zenodo / Software Heritage). The SCM task generator, the cfRNA-ICL model, the meta-training loop, the benchmark harness and the plotting code are all absent. No trained cfRNA-ICL checkpoint is released either, so even inference cannot be repeated.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the SCM generator, model code, training configuration and evaluation harness in a public repository with an archived DOI snapshot, release the trained checkpoint, and add a Code Availability statement.

gaps.missing: Not one software package or version appears anywhere in the paper: no deep-learning framework (PyTorch/JAX/TensorFlow), no numerical or statistics library, no UMAP implementation, no Python or R version. TabICL and TabPFN are cited as arXiv papers, not as pinned dependencies with a commit or release. This is the binding constraint that caps every step at X.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a software table naming and pinning every dependency (language runtime, DL framework + CUDA, umap-learn, numpy/scipy/scikit-learn, and the exact TabICL release or commit used for the baseline).

gaps.missing: No environment lockfile, container image or digest, conda/pip specification, or requirements file is claimed anywhere. There is no dependency closure of any kind, and no hardware description for the meta-training run.
gaps.how_to_close: Provide a container digest or conda-lock/uv.lock covering the full training and evaluation stack, and record the accelerator type and count used for meta-training.

gaps.where: SCM generator (C6, C7), model architecture and meta-training (C9), baseline (C10), evaluation (C11-C13)
gaps.missing: Nearly all numerical settings are symbolic or absent: number of latent factors K, Gaussian loading clipping bounds, structural-equation family mixture weights, MLP/tree sizes, library-size distribution and the CPM scaling constant s; embedding/hidden dimensions, layer and head counts, optimiser, learning rate, batch size, number of meta-training tasks and steps; the TabICL baseline checkpoint and the 'identical fine-tuning procedure'; per-task cohort definitions and preprocessing for the 16 GSE183635 tasks; the few-shot sampling scheme and repeat count; and all UMAP parameters. No random seed is reported for any stochastic step.
gaps.how_to_close: State every hyperparameter in a configuration table (or ship the config files), define each of the 16 benchmark tasks by explicit sample lists, and report seeds and the number of repetitions behind every mean/variance reported.

gaps.where: Methods, first paragraph (cfRNA Codex) and Results (3,079-sample compendium)
gaps.missing: The meta-training calibration data - the cfRNA Codex atlas of >15,000 plasma cfRNA samples and the derived 3,079-sample / 35-study QC-passed compendium - has no accession, no deposit and no access instructions. It is referenced only as a companion preprint DOI (10.13140/RG.2.2.34492.71042, a ResearchGate DOI which returned HTTP 403 to unauthenticated curl). The 35 constituent studies are not enumerated, so the compendium cannot be rebuilt from public sources either.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the harmonised Codex expression matrices (or, at minimum, the per-gene dropout / mean / CV / detect-rate summary statistics that actually parameterise the SCM) in a public archive, and publish the list of 35 constituent studies with their accessions and the QC criteria applied.

gaps.missing: There is no Data Availability statement at all. The downstream benchmark accession GSE183635 appears only as a bibliography entry (reference [19], with a working NCBI GEO URL, accessed 2025-12-10), not as a declared data-availability artifact, and the synthetic task datasets used for meta-training and for the fidelity analysis are not archived.
gaps.how_to_close: Add an explicit Data Availability statement listing GSE183635, the Codex deposit, and an archived snapshot (or generation script plus seed) of the synthetic task universe.

gaps.missing: Modality/identity ambiguity in the benchmark dataset: reference [19] titles GSE183635 'Detection and localization of early- and late-stage cancers using tumor-educated platelet RNA', while the paper describes the K = 16 benchmark tasks as cfRNA classification. Whether the evaluation is on platelet RNA, on a cfRNA subset, or on a re-labelled derivative cannot be determined from the text.
gaps.how_to_close: State explicitly which samples and which assay modality the 16 benchmark tasks are built from, and reconcile the accession with the cfRNA framing.
